findings.claim: The new pre-save vault check is not executable as written. It tells the agent to decide on whether a matching page 'carries engram_id and no memorycard_id', but the query tool does not return page frontmatter. The skill also never says to pass the required `project` argument, nor how to read the page.
evidence: longterm-mem/internal/query/result.go:52-58 defines ResultRow. A vault row carries only sources, rank, page_address, page_path, title and a snippet. engram_id is omitted for vault rows ('A vault row leaves both zero') and there is no memorycard_id field.
longterm-mem/internal/mcpserver/server.go:100-102 makes `project` a required, non-omitempty field of QueryIn. The new text names only `sources: ["vault"]` and the Source-Id.

The frontmatter with engram_id lives only in the page file (/home/labdrian/labdrian-brain/wiki/memory/c-000118.md:15 `engram_id: 3422`; the Source-Id is at line 216, deep in the body). The agent would have to open page_path, and the skill gives no instruction to do so.
A snippet is cut by the vault retriever, so a hit on the Source-Id may not even surface in it.

Consequence: an agent can fail to detect a pre-memorycard page. It then runs mem_save, which overwrites the imported memory, and promote refuses afterwards. That is the exact failure D12 meant to prevent. An agent that guesses may instead block a source that is not bridged.
Read Log L23 and L24 of odd/tasks/phase9-c22-knowledge-ingestion.md in the worktree.

memorycard internal/mcpserver/server.go:96-106: saveArgs has title, body, type, topic_key, scope, supersedes, project, cwd, directory. The new contract note lists supersedes, cwd and directory correctly, and says content is sent as body.
memorycard internal/memory/save.go:206-224: parts titled '(part i/N)', keys <key>/part-i, and the importer variant <key>/part-i~<n>. This matches the new SKILL text.
longterm-mem internal/promote/card.go:77-88: PromoteCard returns BridgedError when scan.bridged is found, before any write. This matches the 'refusal at promote' clause.
c-000118.md has engram_id 3422 and a Source-Id in its body, which supports the D12 premise that such a page can be recognised on the vault side.
The change does not contradict other lines I checked. The SKILL line 145 and 151 vault checks and the contract's supersedes row are consistent. I did not check every other contract line.
